The Planner failed to distinguish between the material composition (minerals) and the structural form (crystals) when evaluating the multiple-choice options, leading to the wrong conclusion. This suggests the question text has a typo. However, the Planner's role was to solve the problem. The Planner concluded C is true based on the search result "Rocks are solid collections of minerals". If the option C says "crystals", the Planner should have noted the discrepancy or selected the option that best fits "minerals". If the option C *in the prompt* actually said "minerals" (and the user typed 'crystals' by mistake in the description but the image/text implies 'minerals'), then the Planner is fine. But based strictly on the text provided: Option C says "crystals". Rocks are made of minerals. Minerals are made of crystals (usually). So "Rocks are made of crystals" is an indirect truth but "Rocks are made of minerals" is the direct definition. The Planner's summary says "Rocks are made up of minerals... If the option text provided to the agent was "crystals", the agent failed to catch that C is technically incorrect or that the option text in the prompt was a typo for "minerals".
